attribution.warning: Messages may be truncated at 1000 characters by the published representative miner; missing visible trailer is not disproof.

llmvul.construction: Published representative miner parses concatenated added diff lines, not complete checked-out files; executed original labeling rules/versions and run logs are unavailable in the retrieved tree.

primevul.limitations: No row-level OneFunc/NVDCheck decision field or local file_info/file_contents package; a CVE or commit link is supporting provenance, not independent function-level validation.

cweval.security_execution: not_run: no Docker executable, no GCC/Clang executable on PATH, and WSL reports not installed; static test mapping is separate evidence
cweval.label_scope: reference versus intentionally unsafe for the specified task/CWE; no universal safety or verified LLM authorship claim

external_review.interpretation: Published rater agreement is source evidence, not our independent adjudication. -1 is undocumented and not recoded. Binary kappa is conditional on omitting incomplete rows.

limitations: No independent new label adjudication; no population label-error estimate.
Structural grouping is a candidate similarity screen, not semantic equivalence or exhaustive fuzzy search.
Sensitivity metrics are descriptive, not causal and not replacement RQ1 scores.
Uncertain LLMVul records have no binary labels or predictions in these analyses.

cweval.limitation: Presence of tests and markers is not a passed test. Duplicate top-level Python definitions can shadow compiled-unsafe wrappers; inspect before execution.

targeted_case_assessments.review_type: single-assistant source-evidence assessment, not independent adjudication

cases.confidence: high for patch-to-function link; no runtime reproduction
cases.evidence: TensorFlow commit 045deec1cbdebb27d817008ad5df94d96a08b1bf adds input_node == nullptr guard immediately before IsSwitch(*input_node) in IsIdentityConsumingSwitch. The dataset function lacks it. Both models predict 0. The local CVE description agrees.

PJSIP patch adds RTCP header-length, padding-length and bit-length guards to pjmedia_rtcp_fb_parse_rpsi. Relevant arithmetic is present in the evaluated function, but header layout and helper contracts are outside it. Both models predict 0. Supplied CWE-200 is not independently adjudicated.

cases.confidence: high for patch link; limited for exploitability
cases.evidence: QEMU patch moves DMA status/message data from FIFO storage to a local two-byte buffer. This supports the change attribution, but does not independently establish null-dereference reachability from the isolated function. Both models predict 0.

Both published raters assign 0; dataset still assigns 1 under tmp.oob-write-index. Exact body and full-file hash match upstream. This is a metrics test main with bounded index loops, but Q38Timers definitions and included qwen38.c contracts remain external. Both model negatives agree with published raters. Do not assert universal safety.

Both published raters assign 0. Exact body and file hash match upstream. p256_transparent_import_key rejects key_buffer_size < data_length before memcpy and validates accepted key sizes. The automated dangerous-memcpy/CWE-120 label is not justified by the copy alone; pointer contracts remain assumed. Both models predict 0.

At the exact recorded commit/file hash, upstream cmd_plan starts with static; dataset starts with atic and appends st from the next function. The published review repairs the initial static but retains the trailing fragment, so its code is not byte-identical. Rater values are -1/1; -1 is undocumented. Published template slices Unicode Python strings using tree-sitter byte offsets, a plausible mechanism, not a verified reconstruction of the mining run.

The complete upstream ACLCheckAllPerm body at the recorded file hash includes a closing brace absent from the dataset. Dataset coordinates 7-12 differ from source start line 1963. VulBERTa's highest-score FP remains a label-relative FP; no corrected-input inference was run in Priority 4.

Exact upstream function uses memcpy(destination, source, min(source_size, sizeof(*destination))). This bounds writes to the destination object under its declared contract. No independent source-read or pointer-contract proof is available. Both models predict 0. Recorded line 1 is actually source line 106; coordinates are not reliable source locations.

Exact upstream unit-test function copies short fixed literals into struct fields. Field capacities live in external declarations. A dangerous-strcpy flag alone does not establish overflow; no safe label is substituted. Both models predict 0.

Both LogFilePrep rows link the same Xorg CVE and commit; their only difference is a comment warning that a user-controlled format string must not run with elevated privileges. No executable-token change supplies the privilege context. VulBERTa probabilities are identical. This is not sufficient to choose which label to overturn.

Vim do_cmdline differs only in two comments, but has opposite labels and different commit references. Each model assigns exactly the same score to both rows. Version-level context may differ; the function alone cannot supply it.

Unsafe function concatenates supplied directory into a popen command. Both models predict 0. The pinned Python test redefines get_ls_result_unsafe, replacing its compiled-C++ wrapper with a Python shell implementation. That unsafe test therefore cannot be claimed to validate the extracted C++ body even if it passes. Reference wrapper is separate.

Pinned security cases reject user_id values containing parent path traversal. Tests compare returned URL strings; they do not perform a network request. The isolated function supports a URL-construction assessment, not independently demonstrated SSRF exploitation.
